description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Evelyn Farkas, former US Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Russia, Ukraine and Eurasia during the Obama administration, says she's skeptical Washington can topple Iran's regime and should instead focus on disabling Tehran's ability to close the Strait of Hormuz. Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey (D) discusses how things are in his city following the withdrawal of thousands of ICE agents who conducted aggressive immigration sweeps. Rep. Beth Van Duyne (R) Texas shares her reaction to higher gas prices and talks about why she believes legislation that has passed will decrease the price of gasoline over time.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Vows to Keep Strait of Hormuz Closed | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/12/2026

description: Rep. Beth Van Duyne (R) Texas shares her reaction to higher gas prices and talks about why she believes legislation that has passed will decrease the price of gasoline over time. She also talks about the partial government shutdown, if Congress is close to agreeing on DHS reforms, and if the SAVE Act can pass. Representative Van Duyne speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Beth Van Duyne on Gas Prices, DHS Reforms, SAVE Act

description: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey (D) discusses how things are in his city following the withdrawal of thousands of ICE agents who conducted aggressive immigration sweeps. Frey states Minneapolis has “been through so much,” and “in recovery mode.” He also shares insight on how small businesses were affected, what his message is to possible new DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin, and his response to Republican messaging changing on deportations. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Minneapolis is in 'Recovery Mode': Mayor Jacob Frey on ICE Withdrawal

description: Evelyn Farkas, former US Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Russia, Ukraine and Eurasia during the Obama administration, says she's skeptical Washington can topple Iran's regime and should instead focus on disabling Tehran's ability to close the Strait of Hormuz. She urges the US must cut a deal for Ukrainian drone defense technology, warning "we need to catch up fast" as modern warfare shifts rapidly. She speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Farkas: US Must Strike Drone Deal With Ukraine as Iran Fight Intensifies

description: President Donald Trump says the situation with Iran is moving along rapidly and doing “very well" during an event at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Situation 'Moving Along Very Rapidly'

author: Katrina Manson
description: An excerpt from the coming book Project Maven shows how the US enlisted Silicon Valley in its vision for AI warfare, now playing out in Iran.
title: ‘God, It’s Terrifying’: How the Pentagon Got Hooked on AI War Machines

author: Galit Altstein, Dan Williams
description: The US-Israeli strikes have significantly weakened Iran and its clerical leadership but cannot guarantee a regime change in the country without an internal uprising, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in his first press briefing since the start of the war.
title: Netanyahu Says No Guarantee of Iran Regime Change After War

author: Olivia Solon, Loni Prinsloo
description: Meta Platforms Inc. has paused part of a massive effort to expand internet service across Africa as the war in the Middle East freezes activity in the region.
title: Work on Massive Meta Cable Project in Persian Gulf Stalled by Iran War

author: Joe Sobczyk
description: Trump and Iranian leader delivered defiant messages on the conflict.
title: Iran War Lines Harden as Effects Ripple Beyond Region

author: Jenny Leonard
description: The US, Japan and the European Union are set to announce plans in the coming weeks to lay the foundation for a trade agreement in critical minerals, according to people familiar with the preparations.
title: US Critical Minerals Talks Advance With EU, Japan on Price Floor

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg Economics chief geoeconomics analyst Jennie Welch on the impact on global energy markets as Iran's supreme leader says that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed. Then, Skyler Weinand, chief investment officer at Regan Capital, discusses market reaction to escalations in the conflict. Plus, Jason Greenblath, senior portfolio manager at American Century Investments, discusses the credit landscape as Amazon drives corporate bond sales to a record single-day high. Finally, Myles Miller gives an update on a shooting at synagogue in West Bloomfield, Michigan. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran's Strait Closure Drives Oil Higher | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/12/2026

author: Gerry Doyle, Galit Altstein, Alberto Nardelli
description: The number of Iranian missile launchers has held steady after a week of unrelenting airstrikes, according to Israeli and western estimates, indicating the difficulty of finding small, mobile targets without having complete control of the skies.
title: Iran’s Missile Launcher Arsenal Holds Steady Despite Strikes

author: Erik Larson, Zoe Tillman
description: The Trump administration said it’s making progress on building a web-based portal to handle refund requests for almost $170 billion in global tariffs that were overturned by the US Supreme Court.
title: US Tells Judge Web-Based Portal for IEEPA Refunds 70% Complete

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, former Israeli Ambassador to the US Michael Oren, Maywood Strategies Principal Doug Farrar and Senator Elissa Slotkin. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US, Iran Strike Defiant Tones | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/12/2026

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Giorgia Meloni urged Italians to back her plans to revamp the courts in a vote that’s effectively become a referendum on the prime minister herself.
title: Meloni Makes Case for Court Revamp Before Crucial Referendum

author: Agnieszka Barteczko, Piotr Bujnicki
description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki said he won’t sign a legislation designed to give his country a quick access to €43.7 billion ($50.3 billion) from the European Union’s loans-for-weapons program in a blow to pro-EU government.
title: Polish President Vetoes Plan to Tap Defense Loans From EU

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The Trump administration imposed new sanctions on six individuals and two entities involved in using North Korean overseas information technology workers to defraud US businesses and funnel hundreds of millions of dollars to Pyongyang’s weapons development.
title: US Imposes Sanctions Over North Korean Fraud Targeting US Firms

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Pentagon testing office said it won’t get enough data to evaluate the combat effectiveness of the US’s first hypersonic missile until early next year, another troubling sign as the US struggles to catch up with China and Russia in deploying the weapon.
title: Pentagon Test Office Needs More Data On New Hypersonic Missile

author: Chris Dolmetsch
description: A judge dismissed most of a lawsuit against the Trump administration for freezing money earmarked for the Gateway tunnel under the Hudson River, after the US government made the disputed payments and work resumed on the $16 billion project.
title: NY-NJ Tunnel-Funding Lawsuit Largely Dismissed After Funds Paid

description:
Earlier on Thursday, Mojtaba Khamenei said the Islamic Republic would seek to ensure the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed. In his first public comments since succeeding his father, he added that Tehran will look to open other fronts in the war if the US and Israel persist with their attacks. 
Oil prices rose more than 10% on Thursday with Brent crude once again briefly topping $100 a barrel as traders generally viewed the Trump administration’s efforts to lower energy costs as mostly temporary. Aaron David Miller, Senior Fellow at Carnegie Endowment for International Peace joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Threatens New Targets; US Works to Tame Oil Prices

author: Erik Larson
description: Two dozen US states asked a judge to expedite their lawsuit challenging the 10% global tariff President Donald Trump imposed last month after the Supreme Court ruled many of his earlier levies unconstitutional.
title: States Ask to Fast-Track Suit Over Trump’s 10% Global Tariff

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Alberto Nardelli, Ellen Milligan
description: Russian intelligence support for Iran’s deadly retaliation against the US, Israel and Gulf allies — as well as concerns China may also be helping Tehran — demonstrates deepening ties among US adversaries as the war with Iran continues to widen.
title: Putin’s ‘Hidden Hand’ Guides Iran’s Strikes in Widening War

author: Beatriz Reis, Daniel Carvalho, Martha Viotti Beck
description: Brazil’s government is moving to shield consumers from surging oil prices worldwide by cutting federal taxes on the import and sale of fuels, while introducing a levy on crude oil exports to offset the revenue loss.
title: Brazil Cuts Fuel Tax to Offset Oil Price Surge as Iran War Rages On

author: Michal Kubala
description: The US dialed up pressure on the Czech Republic after billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis’s government pushed through a budget that fell short of NATO defense-spending targets.
title: US Envoy Heaps Pressure on Czechs to Boost Defense Spending

author: Dana Khraiche, Youssef Diab
description: Israel said it’s preparing to expand an incursion into southern Lebanon to fight Iran-backed Hezbollah militants, an escalation that threatens a humanitarian crisis and regional repercussions amid the ongoing Iran war.
title: Israel Expands War on Hezbollah in Lebanon as Crisis Grows

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump and Iran’s new supreme leader both struck defiant tones on the 13th day of the war, offering little relief to energy markets as Brent crude briefly topped $100 barrel despite fresh US efforts to curb oil prices.
title: Trump and Iran Strike Defiant Tone as Oil Markets See Little Relief

author: Alastair Gale, Philip Heijmans, Yian Lee
description: When the US pulled its only aircraft carrier based in Asia to support the military surge in Afghanistan back in 2010, allies in the region had little concern that China or North Korea might look to take advantage. Today things are different.
title: US Allies Near China on Edge as Weapons Shift From Asia to Iran

author: Katy O'Donnell
description: The US Senate on Thursday passed a bipartisan bill aimed at boosting the nation’s supply of homes on an 89-10 vote, setting up a showdown in the House over a contentious provision to limit Wall Street’s footprint in the housing market.
title: Senate Passes Housing Bill With Trump Investor Ban, Setting Up Clash in House

author: Mark Schroers
description: The European Central Bank is confronting the threat of another bout of war-induced inflation in the knowledge that this time is probably different, and it’s better positioned to respond.
title: Europe’s Price Shock Is Still a Long Way From 2022 Energy Crisis

author: Jake Bleiberg, John Tozzi
description: A cyberattack on Stryker Corp. has kept the medical technology company’s ordering and shipping systems offline as the firm continues to struggle to address a crippling hack claimed by a group linked to Iran.
title: Stryker Shipping Still Down in Attack Claimed by Pro-Iran Group

author: Maggie Eastland
description: Dell Technologies Inc. Chief Executive Officer Michael Dell said that a company doing business with the government can’t tell agencies how to use its technology, responding to a question about Anthropic PBC’s feud with the US Defense Department.
title: Dell Says Companies Can’t Tell Government How to Use Their Tech

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US President Donald Trump said it would not be “appropriate” for Iran to participate in this summer’s World Cup being staged in North America, though he left the door open for its team to play.
title: Trump Says Iran Shouldn’t Play in World Cup for Team’s ‘Safety’

author: Eliyahu Kamisher, Biz Carson
description: Silicon Valley billionaires have been seething over the threat of more taxes and regulations at home. Now, a proposed nine-figure fund aims to give wealthy Californians an unprecedented tool to reshape the state’s politics in their favor.
title: Ultrawealthy Consider $500 Million Fund to Influence California Politics

author: Zahra Hirji
description: The shutdown of the US Department of Homeland Security has thrust into limbo a long-awaited report on how to revamp the nation’s top disaster agency, according to one of the report authors.
title: DHS Shutdown Puts High-Profile Report on FEMA in Limbo

author: Golnar Motevalli, Patrick Sykes, Arsalan Shahla
description: Residents of Tehran say they are caught between bombs and security forces warning of a swift crackdown on any dissent.
title: Under a Blackened Sky, Iranians Navigate War and Regime Threats

author: Alicia Tang
description: Palantir Technologies Inc. may turn to other AI models amid the spat between Anthropic PBC and the Pentagon.
title: Palantir Looks to Expand Beyond Anthropic After Pentagon Spat

author: Ellen Milligan, Gerry Doyle
description: It’s becoming increasingly evident that Iran is laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the UK, as Iran’s new supreme leader used his first comments to the media to say the critical waterway should stay closed.
title: Iran Likely Mining Hormuz as Khamenei Squeezes Strait, UK Says

author: Amanda Albright, Laura Nahmias
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was hit with a string of warnings this week about the city’s finances, as he tries to enact ambitious campaign promises while contending with a gloomy fiscal reality.
title: NYC’s Mamdani Confronts Warnings on City’s Financial Issues

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Ari Natter
description: The Trump administration plans to waive a century-old maritime law that requires American ships be used to transport goods between US ports as it seeks to blunt surging oil and gasoline prices, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: US to Ease Ship Rule in Bid to Tame Spiraling Fuel Prices

author: Roxana Tiron
description: US officials told lawmakers that the first six days of the war with Iran cost more than $11.3 billion, a person familiar with the matter said, giving the most detailed assessment yet of the expense involved in President Donald Trump’s military campaign.
title: US Spent $11.3 Billion in First Week of War With Iran

description: France’s far-right National Rally is eyeing a Marseille municipal win as a springboard to the 2027 presidential race, as Caroline Connan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why Marseille Matters in France's 2027 Presidential Vote

description: Iran's new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said the Strait of Hormuz should stay closed and new fronts in the war will be opened if the US and Israel continue their attacks. These were the first public statements made by Khamenei since succeeding his father four days ago. Bloomberg Opinion's Marc Champion joins Bloomberg Open Interest with more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran's New Supreme Leader Says Strait of Hormuz Should Stay Closed

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungarian opposition leader Peter Magyar held a series of rallies in towns that host controversial battery plants a month before a key election, seeking to hone a message on an issue that’s damaged Prime Minister Viktor Orban.
title: Magyar Holds Rallies in Battery Towns to Shift Hungary Election Focus from Ukraine War

author: Ewa Krukowska, Alberto Nardelli, Jorge Valero
description: The European Commission is considering relaxing carbon-permit supply rules and allowing more state aid as part of an emergency plan to cut spiking power prices, according to people familiar with the plans.
title: EU Weighs Looser Carbon Rules and State Aid to Cut Energy Prices

author: Eltaf Najafizada, Patrick Sykes, Paul Wallace
description: Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said the Strait of Hormuz should remain closed and signaled he won’t back down in the Middle East war, in his first public comments since succeeding his assassinated father.
title: Iran’s New Supreme Leader Khamenei Says Hormuz Strait Should Stay Closed

author: Bilal Hussain
description: Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will travel to Saudi Arabia to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Thursday, a day after speaking with Iran’s president about the deteriorating situation in the Middle East.
title: Pakistan’s PM Heads to Saudi Arabia After Talks With Iran Leader

author: Ted Mann
description: Since last year, the railroad industry has been in a panic. A small group of officials in the Trump administration was trying to revive a slate of safety proposals, first raised after the 2023 East Palestine, Ohio, train derailment, that railroads say would dramatically drive up their operating costs.
title: Vance Allies’ Railway Proposals Hint at Populist 2028 Playbook

author: Adelaide Changole
description: Sanlam Ltd. sounded the alarm about the impact of a protracted war in the Middle East, with Africa’s biggest insurer saying the conflict could have a “massive” impact on its performance.
title: Top Africa Insurer Sanlam Flags ‘Massive’ Risks From Iran War

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: The US Navy could start escorting tankers through the Strait of Hormuz by the end of this month, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said, while President Donald Trump signaled he sees some benefits from the global oil price surge.
title: US Eyes Hormuz Escorts by April as Trump Downplays Oil Spike

author: Ewa Krukowska, Lyubov Pronina, Laura Noonan
description: The European Union’s economic heavyweights are urging the bloc to reduce its dependency on foreign payments systems and accelerate the digital euro’s rollout as they seek to boost Europe’s productivity and growth.
title: EU Countries Call for Stronger European Payments Systems

description: Iran stepped up attacks on parts of Dubai and shipping assets in the Persian Gulf, heightening concern about the length of the Middle East war and the impact on already volatile energy markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Escalates Attacks on Dubai and Shipping, Rattling Markets

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union rebuffed US allegations that it’s contributing to global market overcapacity, and vowed to respond “firmly and proportionally” if Washington imposes tariffs that breach a trade deal with the bloc.
title: EU Rejects US Trade Probe Allegations of Market Overcapacity

description: Video shows the aftermath of a drone falling on a building in Dubai Creek Harbour, a new development of residential towers. The authorities said they quickly had the resulting fire under control and there were no casualties reported. (Source: Associated Press)
title: Dubai Creek Harbour Building Damaged by Drone

author: Anthony Halpin
description: A Kremlin envoy met Trump officials in Florida yesterday to discuss the energy crisis.
title: Putin Grabs Opportunity From Global Oil Chaos

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia plans to scale back this year’s budget spending to rein in a widening deficit and avoid an increase in borrowing, even as surging oil prices boost revenue.
title: Russia to Slash Spending Even as Iran War Boosts Oil Prices

author: Laura Millan, Eric Roston
description: Climate-fueled drought and mismanagement have left the country with a severe water shortage, and war only adds to the strain.
title: War Is Pushing Iran’s Water Supply to the Brink of Collapse

author: Eltaf Najafizada, Dan Williams
description: Iran escalated attacks on parts of Dubai and shipping assets, pushing oil prices above $100 a barrel and causing more concern about the length of the Middle East war and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Iran Escalates Attacks on Dubai and Shipping, Sending Oil Higher

description: President Donald Trump’s administration started the first of several sweeping trade investigations that set the stage for new tariffs, the centerpiece of a push to replace levies struck down by the US Supreme Court. Trading partners that will be subject to the inquiry include China, the European Union, Mexico and India. Bloomberg's Jill Disis reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Trade Probe Into China Paves Way for New Trump Tariffs

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, Brent rallied back to the $100 level after Oman cleared all ships from its key export oil terminal and two tankers were attacked in Iraqi waters. 

US President Donald Trump vowed to “finish the job” in the campaign against Iran. 

The Trump administration started investigations into trading partners including the EU, China and India, setting the stage for new tariffs.

Today's guests: Sophie Huynh, Portfolio Manager and Strategist in Dynamic Asset Allocation at BNP Paribas Asset Management & Citi EMEA Technology Investment Banking Co-Head Amit Nayyar (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Tanker Attacks Spike Oil & Trump Trade Probe | Daybreak Europe 03/12/2026

author: Charlie Zhu, Jing Li
description: China adopted a law cementing President Xi Jinping’s push to assimilate the country’s ethnic minorities, another shift away from Beijing’s long-held policy of giving such groups at least symbolic autonomy.
title: China Passes Ethnic Unity Law to Advance Xi’s Assimilation Push

author: Alastair Gale, Sakura Murakami
description: Japan’s pacifist constitution wouldn’t bar the country from helping with mine clearance around the Strait of Hormuz at the conclusion of the war between the US, Israel and Iran, but Tokyo has no plans to deploy minesweepers to the region, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said.
title: Japan Isn’t Sending Minesweepers to Middle East, Takaichi Says

author: Matthew Hill, Tavares Cebola
description: The European Union’s financial support for Rwandan troops helping to fight an Islamic State-linked insurgency in Mozambique expires in May and there are no plans to extend it, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: EU Funding for Rwanda’s Mozambique Deployment Set to End in May

description: France's far-right National Rally is targeting a win in the southern city of Marseille in forthcoming municipal elections. Marine Le Pen's once taboo party sees a victory in the cosmopolitan, diverse metropolis as a potential stepping stone to winning the 2027 presidential election. Bloomberg's Caroline Connan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Marseille Has Become a Target for France's Far Right

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev said he discussed the crisis in global energy markets at talks with US officials in Florida.
title: Putin Envoy Says He Discussed Energy Crisis With Trump Officials

author: Yian Lee, Alastair Gale
description: China sent more military aircraft into a sensitive area off Taiwan following a brief period that saw it mysteriously hold off on the flights.
title: China Sends More Warplanes Toward Taiwan After Mystery Lull

author: Ania Nussbaum
description: Nathalie Prevost is fed up. She makes her living selling paella at Marseille’s Michelet market, but authorities’ failure to stamp out petty crime has left her so frustrated she didn’t bother to file a police report after her cash box was recently stolen.
title: Le Pen’s Crossover Appeal Is Put to the Test in Marseille Voting

author: Randy Thanthong-Knight
description: Thailand denounced the attack on a Thai-flagged vessel in the Strait of Hormuz and summoned Iran’s ambassador, as authorities race to rescue three crew members feared trapped aboard the damaged ship.
title: Thailand Condemns Hormuz Ship Strike, Summons Iran Ambassador

author: Leah Nylen
description: Two Live Nation Entertainment Inc. executives bragged about the high fees the company charges fans at its venues, joking in internal messages that the company is “robbing them blind” and that “these people are so stupid” that “I almost feel bad taking advantage of them.”
title: Live Nation Can ‘Gouge’ Fans on Fees, Ticketing Executives Boast

description: A UAE navy vessel patrols next to cargo ships and oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz as seen from Khor Fakkan, United Arab Emirates, on March 11. Photographer: Altaf Qadri/AP Photo
title: Oil Hits $100 as Shipping Turmoil Intensifies

author: Matthew Malinowski, Antonia Mufarech
description: Chile’s new President José Antonio Kast signed decrees to ramp up border security, audit spending and cut red tape before delivering a tightly scripted inaugural speech on Wednesday night, underscoring his priorities at the helm of Latin America’s most prosperous nation.
title: Chile’s New President Brings Back Tie in Vow to Restore Order

author: Tooba Khan, Jorgelina Do Rosario
description: Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund will continue discussions over another round of funding from a $7 billion bailout program aimed at restoring confidence in the country’s economy, amid questions on how the ongoing war in Iran may impact its eastern neighbor.
title: IMF, Pakistan Extend Talks Amid Questions on Iran War Impact

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Republican Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky speaks about the costs of war, ICE agents wearing masks, and confirming Markwayne Mullin as the next Homeland Security secretary. Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin signals she won’t support supplemental funding for the Pentagon without a clearer breakdown of how existing defense dollars are being spent. Senator Tina Smith (D) Minnesota discusses needing ICE to change their tactics in order to reopen DHS and shares the latest on the Senate housing bill. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Signals US Will Tap Oil Reserve | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/11/2026
